def M_PrimitiveArrayData : ArrayRefParameter<"uint8_t",
    "aligned storage for primitive elements"> {
  let allocator = [{
    $_dst = copyIntoAlignedBuffer($_allocator, $_self, elementType);
  }];
  let cppStorageType = "std::vector<uint8_t>";
}

def M_PrimitiveArrayAttr : MAttr<"PrimitiveArray", "primitives_array"> {
  let summary = "an array of primitive elements";
  let description = [{
    The `#M.primitives_array` attribute represents an array of primitive
    (boolean, integer, index, or floating point) data of equal size. The data is
    stored as a byte array with element types whose sizes are not multiples of
    bytes padded to the nearest byte. The underlying array is aligned to that
    byte size.

    Example:

    ```mlir
    // An array of integers.
    #M.primitives_array<si24: -2, 0, 2>

    // An array of floats.
    #M.primitives_array<bf16: 0.2, 1.2, 3.>

    // Boolean arrays use `i1` elements.
    #M.primitives_array<i1: true, false, true>
    ```
  }];

  let parameters = (ins M_PrimitiveArrayData:$data, "Type":$elementType);
  let assemblyFormat = [{
    `<` $elementType `` custom<PrimitiveArray>($data, ref($elementType)) `>`
  }];
  let genVerifyDecl = 1;

  let builders = [
    AttrBuilderWithInferredContext<(ins "ArrayRef<uint8_t>":$data,
                                        "Type":$elementType)>
  ];

  let extraClassDeclaration = [{
    /// Return the number of elements.
    int64_t size() const;
  }];
}

//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
// ArrayElementsAttr
//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//

def M_ArrayElementsAttr : MAttr<"ArrayElements", "dense_array",
    [ElementsAttrInterface, TypedAttrInterface,
     DeclareAttrInterfaceMethods<HasAlignedBytesInterface, ["getAlignedBytesType"]>]> {
  let summary = "an elements attribute backed by an array";
  let description = [{
    The `#M.dense_array` attribute is an elements attribute backed by a
    primitive array. The attribute supports the full API expected by
    `ElementsAttr` and users thereof, including arbitrary shaped types and
    failable value iteration.

    Importantly, this attribute can only contain scalar integer and floating
    point types, does not bit-pack elements, and does not have special handling
    for splat elements.

    This attribute implements the HasAlignedBytesInterface by returning a
    !M.aligned_bytes type capturing the byte size of the underlying element data
    array and an alignment of the next power-of-two of the byte size of the
    element type.

    Example:

    ```mlir
    // An array of integers.
    #M.dense_array<-3, 0, 1, 42> : !M.array<4xi32>

    // A float tensor.
    #M.dense_array<3.4, 2.3, 5.2, 1.9> : tensor<2x2xf32>

    // A 0D vector.
    #M.dense_array<1> : vector<ui64>
    ```
  }];

  let parameters = (ins "PrimitiveArrayAttr":$data,
                        AttributeSelfTypeParameter<"", "ShapedType">:$type);
  let genVerifyDecl = 1;
  let hasCustomAssemblyFormat = 1;

  let builders = [
    AttrBuilderWithInferredContext<(ins "ArrayRef<uint8_t>":$data,
                                        "ShapedType":$type)>
  ];

  let extraClassDeclaration = [{
    /// Get the raw underlying data.
    ArrayRef<uint8_t> getRawData() const;

    /// `ElementsAttr` implementation. Support iteration with `Attribute` to be
    /// compatible with upstream dialects.
    using NonContiguousIterableTypesT = std::tuple<Attribute>;
    FailureOr<detail::AttrIterator>
    try_value_begin_impl(OverloadToken<Attribute>) const;
  }];
}

//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
// AlignedBytesAttr
//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//

// Make sure the attribute's data argument is interned with the requested
// alignment.
def M_AlignedBytesData : ArrayRefParameter<"uint8_t",
    "aligned storage for AlignedBytesAttr"> {
  let allocator = [{
    $_dst = copyIntoBytes($_allocator, $_self, align);
  }];
}

def M_AlignedBytesAttr : MAttr<"AlignedBytes", "aligned_bytes", [
    DeclareAttrInterfaceMethods<ElementsAttrInterface>,
    DeclareAttrInterfaceMethods<HasAlignedBytesInterface, ["getAlignedBytesType"]>]> {
  let summary = "A literal byte array with alignment.";
  let description = [{
    This attribute is the 'inline' equivalent of `dense_resource`, and describes
    a byte array with byte alignment. Nothing is implied about the internal
    structure of the bytes (rank, dimensions, underlying element type, padding,
    or element endianness).

    This attribute implements the ElementsAttrInterface as a rank-1 ShapedType
    over uint8_t elements.

    This attribute implements the HasAlignedBytesInterface by returning the
    obvious !M.aligned_bytes type.

    Generally this attribute should only be used for 'small' literals. Larger
    literals should be placed into the resources table and be referenced by the
    `dense_resources` attribute. Note that dense resources encode their
    alignment in their first four bytes using the little-endian convention,
    where as this attribute describes the alignment explicitly.

    Examples:
    ```mlir
    #M.aligned_bytes<"0x01020304", align 64> // 4 bytes, aligned on 64 bytes
    ```
  }];

  let parameters = (ins M_AlignedBytesData:$data, "uint64_t":$align);
  let assemblyFormat = [{
    `<` custom<AlignedBytesData>($data) `,` `align` $align `>`
  }];
  let genVerifyDecl = 1;

  let extraClassDeclaration = [{
    /// ElementsAttr interface implementation.
    using ContiguousIterableTypesT = std::tuple<uint8_t>;
    FailureOr<const uint8_t*> try_value_begin_impl(OverloadToken<uint8_t>) const;
    ShapedType getType() const;
  }];
}

def M_MultiLineStringAttr
    : ArrayOfAttr<MDialect, "MultiLineString", "multiline", "StringAttr"> {
  let summary = "An array of strings which is encoded as a multi-line "
                "null-terminated string in MEF.";
  let description = [{
    An array of strings.

    Encoded into MEF as a multi-line null-terminated string using `\n` as
    the line terminator.

    Example: The attribute
    ```mlir
      #m<multiline["line1",
                   "line2"]>
    ```
    will appear in MEF as the the string "line1\nline2\n\0".
  }];
}

//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
// TargetInfoAttr
//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//

def OptionalStringRefParameter : StringRefParameter<""> {
  let defaultValue = "\"\"";
}

def OptionalDataLayoutParameter : AttrParameter<"DataLayout", "data layout", "const DataLayout &"> {
  let defaultValue = "DataLayout()";
}

def M_TargetInfoAttr : MAttr<"TargetInfo", "target"> {
  let summary = "Target configuration attribute.";
  let description = [{
    The `#M.target` attribute represents a compilation target configuration. It
    contains the target triple, microarchitecture, stdlib plugin, optional features,
    and derived data such as data layout and SIMD width.

    The user can also specify the default index bit width being used. This is
    important for GPUs where the hardware can support different index bit widths
    for cross compilation.

    The microarchitecture and features may encode version numbers, such as
    'sm_80' for CUDA compute capability 8.0. When deciding if a runtime host
    supports a compile time microarchitecutre or feature it may be necessary
    to compare these versions numerically rather than textually.

    Features are encoded in the form of "+feature1,+feature2,-feature3",
    where "+" enables and "-" disables a feature. The list is fully
    expanded: it includes both the features explicitly requested by the
    user and all features enabled by default for the target CPU (e.g.
    avx512f on znver4), with explicit user overrides applied on top.
    A feature present in the list without a "-" entry is enabled; a
    feature absent from the list was not enabled by the CPU model and
    was not explicitly requested.

    Example:
    ```mlir
    #M.target<triple="x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu", arch="znver3",
              stdlib_plugin="default", features="+avx,+avx2",
              data_layout="p:64:64-i64:64:64", relocation_model="static",
              simd_bit_width=256, index_bit_width=64>
    #M.target<triple="nvptx64-nvidia-cuda", arch="sm_80", stdlib_plugin="cuda">
    ```

    Can be (partially) represented at runtime by M::TargetInfo.

    The `accelerator_arch` contains the vendor name of the accelerator in
    lowercase (e.g. nvidia or amd) along with the compute capability (e.g. 80 or
    90). For example, a valid `accelerator_arch` is `nvidia:80` or `amdgpu:gfx942`.

    The `abi` names the target ABI (e.g. RISC-V's `lp64d`, MIPS's `n32`),
    mirroring clang's `-target-abi`. When set, it is recorded as a
    `target-abi` LLVM module flag, exactly as clang does.

    The `opaque_plugin` carries an opaque payload as the stdlib plugin. MDialect
    never inspects it. The payload must be a typed attribute, so that its type
    is always available to the dialect that interprets it.

    Example:
    ```mlir
    #M.target<triple="x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu", arch="znver3",
              opaque_plugin=#kgen.param_list<index>
                          : !kgen.param_list<!kgen.type>>
    ```
  }];

  let parameters = (ins
    "llvm::Triple":$triple,
    StringRefParameter<>:$arch,
    StringRefParameter<"", "\"default\"">:$stdlib_plugin,
    OptionalParameter<"TypedAttr">:$opaque_plugin,
    OptionalStringRefParameter:$features,
    OptionalDataLayoutParameter:$data_layout,
    DefaultValuedParameter<"llvm::Reloc::Model",
                           "llvm::Reloc::Static">:$relocation_model,
    DefaultValuedParameter<"int64_t", "0">:$simd_bit_width,
    DefaultValuedParameter<"std::optional<int64_t>",
                           "std::nullopt">:$index_bit_width,
    OptionalStringRefParameter:$tune_cpu,
    OptionalStringRefParameter:$accelerator_arch,
    OptionalStringRefParameter:$abi
  );

  let assemblyFormat = "`<` struct(params) `>`";

  let extraClassDeclaration = [{
    /// Get the target triple as a string.
    std::string getTripleStr() const {
      return getTriple().normalize();
    }

    /// Returns whether the triple is a GPU target.
    bool isGPU() const {
      return getTriple().isNVPTX() || getTriple().isAMDGPU() || isMetal();
    }

    /// Returns whether this is a Metal target (macOS with actual GPU, not embedded devices).
    bool isMetal() const {
      // Use the same logic as isMetalTriple() for consistency
      // Accept both air64 and arm64 triples for Metal GPU targets
      return getTripleStr().starts_with("air64");
    }

    /// Check if the target supports a specific hardware feature.
    /// See M::hasFeature for the matching contract.
    bool hasFeature(StringRef feature) const {
      return M::hasFeature(getFeatures(), feature);
    }

    /// Returns the operating system for the triple.
    StringRef getOS() const {
      return llvm::Triple::getOSTypeName(getTriple().getOS());
    }

    /// Returns the resolved index_bit_width.
    int64_t resolveIndexBitWidth() {
      return getIndexBitWidth().value_or(getDataLayout().getPointerBitWidth());
    }

    /// Returns ptr byteSize for the interpreter which is always 8
    int32_t getDefaultPointerSize() {
      return 8;
    }
  }];
}

//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
// DeviceRefAttr
//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//

def M_DeviceRefAttr : MAttr<"DeviceRef", "device_ref"> {
  let summary = "Refers to a device spec a value or operation occupies";
  let description = [{
    The `#M.device_ref` attribute refers to a unique `#M.device_spec` within the
    overall model `#M.device_spec_collection`. It contain a label and id.

    Example:
    ```mlir
      #M.device_ref<"gpu", 0>
    ```
  }];

  let parameters = (ins
    StringRefParameter<>:$label,
    "DeviceId":$id
  );

  let constBuilderCall = "M::DeviceRefAttr::get($_builder.getContext(), $0)";

  let assemblyFormat = [{
    `<` $label `,` $id `>`
  }];

  let extraClassDeclaration = [{
    /// Returns device ref in compact string form.
    std::string toString() const;

    /// Returns the default M.device_ref<"cpu", 0> device ref.
    static DeviceRefAttr getDefault(mlir::MLIRContext* ctx);
  }];
}

//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
// DeviceRefArrayAttr
//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//

def M_DeviceRefArrayAttr : TypedArrayAttrBase<M_DeviceRefAttr, "A list of devicerefs">;

//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
// DeviceRefsAttr
//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//

def M_DeviceRefsAttr
    : ArrayOfAttr<MDialect, "DeviceRefs", "devices", "DeviceRefAttr">;

//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
// DeviceInfoAttr
//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//

def M_DeviceInfoAttr : MAttr<"DeviceInfo", "device_info"> {
  let summary = "Runtime-probed information about a physical device";
  let description = [{
    The `#M.device_info` attribute captures runtime-probed properties of a
    physical device: its label (e.g. `"gpu"`), the underlying API
    (e.g. `"cuda"`, `"hip"`), the architecture name
    (e.g. `"sm_100a"`, `"gfx942"`), and the model name
    (e.g. `"NVIDIA B200"`). This is used to drive per-kernel device
    registration and specialization.

    Example:
    ```mlir
      #M.device_info<"gpu", "cuda", "sm_100a", "NVIDIA B200">
    ```
  }];

  let parameters = (ins
    StringRefParameter<>:$label,
    StringRefParameter<>:$api,
    StringRefParameter<>:$arch,
    StringRefParameter<>:$model,
    DefaultValuedParameter<"bool", "false">:$tile_based_fusion
  );

  let assemblyFormat = [{
    `<` $label `,` $api `,` $arch `,` $model
    (`,` `tile_based_fusion` `=` $tile_based_fusion^)? `>`
  }];
}

//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
// DeviceSpecAttr
//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//

def M_DeviceSpecAttr : MAttr<"DeviceSpec", "device_spec"> {
  let summary = "Compile-time information about a computational device.";
  let description = [{
    The `#M.device_spec` attribute describes everything we need to know about a
    computational device at compile time which is expected to be present at
    runtime. This includes the device's `#M.target` configuration (to guide
    code generation), the device's id (to disambiguate the device from other
    devices with similar target configuration, default 0), and a string label
    (so model types and ops may refer to a specific device when needed, eg for
    device placement).

    Device ids need not refer to physical devices (eg a specific CUDA device
    id), they are just placeholders. It is the responsibility of the various
    setup ops in the model's 'init' block to establish the mapping from device
    ids used in the model to actual physical devices where required. This may
    require matching properties of the `#M.target` to capabilities probed at
    runtime.

    ```mlir
    #M.device_spec<ref = <"gpu", 1>,
                   target = <triple="nvptx64-nvidia-cuda", arch="sm_80">>
    ```

    Can be represented at runtime by M::DeviceSpec.
  }];

  let parameters = (ins
    M_DeviceRefAttr:$ref,
    M_TargetInfoAttr:$target
  );

  let assemblyFormat = "`<` struct(params) `>`";
}

//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
// DeviceSpecCollectionAttr
//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//

def M_DeviceSpecCollectionAttr : MAttr<"DeviceSpecCollection", "device_spec_collection"> {
  let summary = "A collection of device specifications.";
  let description = [{
    The `#M.device_spec_collection` attribute describes a collection of
    `#M.device_spec` attributes along with the device reference for the
    unique 'host' device. Each `#M.device_spec` must have a distinct device
    reference, and obviously the 'host' device reference must exist.

    ```mlir
    #M.device_spec_collection<
      host = <"cpu", 0>,
      devices = [<ref = <"cpu", 0>,
                  target = <triple="x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu", arch="znver3",
                            features="+avx2">>,
                 <ref = <"gpu", 1>,
                  target = <triple="nvptx64-nvidia-cuda", arch="sm_80">>]>
    ```

    Encoded into MEF as JSON in string form.

    Can be represented at runtime by M::DeviceSpecCollection.
  }];

  let parameters = (ins
    M_DeviceRefAttr:$host,
    ArrayRefParameter<"DeviceSpecAttr">:$devices
  );

  let assemblyFormat = [{
    `<` `host` `=` $host `,` `devices` `=` custom<DeviceSpecAttrArray>($devices) `>`
  }];

  let extraClassDeclaration = [{
    /// Returns the device spec which matches device reference, or an error if
    /// no match.
    ErrorOr<DeviceSpecAttr> findDeviceSpec(DeviceRefAttr deviceReference) const;

    /// Returns the device spec for the host.
    DeviceSpecAttr getHostDeviceSpec() const;
  }];

  let genVerifyDecl = 1;
}

//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
// InOutSignatureAttr
//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//

def M_InOutSignatureAttr : MAttr<"InOutSignature", "inout_sig"> {
  let summary = "Describes the in/out/mut intended semantics for "
                "pointer-like operands.";
  let description = [{
    This attribute captures the intended semantics for each pointer-like
    operand of a primitive or kernel.
     - '.': Operand is a value.
     - 'i': Operand is only read.
     - 'o': Operand is only written.
     - 'm': Operand is mutated in-place.

    May be used to distinguish buffer-like operands on generic ops during
    compilation, in which case the attribute can be erased before conversion
    to MEF etc. May also be made available at runtime to help in runtime
    assertions and safety checks.

    Encoded into MEF as a string.

    Example:
    ```mlir
    #M.inout_sig<"ii.mo">
    ```
  }];

  let parameters = (ins StringRefParameter<>:$signature);
  let assemblyFormat = "`<` $signature `>`";
  let genVerifyDecl = 1;

  let extraClassDeclaration = [{
     /// The in/out/mut semantics of a single operand.
     enum InOutSemantics : char {
       kNone = '.',
       kIn = 'i',
       kOut = 'o',
       kMut = 'm'
     };

     /// Returns the arity of the signature.
     size_t size() const { return getSignature().size(); }

     /// Returns the semantics for the i'th operand.
     InOutSemantics operator[](size_t i) const {
       const StringRef& sig = getSignature();
       assert(i < sig.size() && "operand index out of range");
       return static_cast<InOutSemantics>(sig[i]);
     }

     /// Returns a new signature attribute with the specified arguments removed.
     InOutSignatureAttr remove(const llvm::BitVector& toRemove);

     /// Append new arguments to the current signature and return the result
     /// as a new signature attribute.
     InOutSignatureAttr append(ArrayRef<InOutSemantics> newArgs);
  }];

  let builders = [
    AttrBuilder<(ins "ArrayRef<InOutSemantics>":$signature)>
  ];
}

#ifndef SDK_GRAPHAPI_PYTHON_CHECKED_H
#define SDK_GRAPHAPI_PYTHON_CHECKED_H

#include "_core/Graph/Bindings.h"
#include "mlir/IR/Diagnostics.h"
#include "mlir/IR/MLIRContext.h"
#include "nanobind/nanobind.h"

namespace M::Graph::Python {

/// RAII scope guard for registering an emit function to pass to verifiers.
/// If the emitter is used, this will raise a corresponding Python error.
struct RaisingScopedEmitFn {
  using EmitFn = llvm::function_ref<mlir::InFlightDiagnostic()>;
  std::string err;
  mlir::MLIRContext *ctx;
  mlir::ScopedDiagnosticHandler handler;
  llvm::unique_function<mlir::InFlightDiagnostic()> emitFn;
  RaisingScopedEmitFn() : RaisingScopedEmitFn(current_context()) {}
  RaisingScopedEmitFn(mlir::MLIRContext *ctx)
      : ctx(ctx),
        handler(ctx, [&](mlir::Diagnostic &diag) { err = diag.str(); }),
        emitFn(mlir::detail::getDefaultDiagnosticEmitFn(ctx)) {}
  ~RaisingScopedEmitFn() noexcept(false) {
    if (!err.empty()) {
      PyErr_Format(PyExc_TypeError, "%s", err.c_str());
      throw nanobind::python_error();
    }
  }
  operator EmitFn() { return emitFn; }
};

/// Function decorator which takes a verify- or getChecked-like function
/// which takens in an emit function (`mlir::InFlightDiagnostic()`)
/// and returns a function which omits that argument, using
/// `RaisingScopedEmitFn` to inject an appropriate emit function and
/// raise in python if it emits.
///
/// The implementation is a recursive template function which creates
/// curried wrappers until it either runs out of arguments, in which case
/// it returns the function, or finds the emit function in which case
/// it returns the injecting function.
template <typename T, typename Arg, typename... Rest>
constexpr auto checked(T (*f)(Arg, Rest...)) {
  using EmitFn = llvm::function_ref<mlir::InFlightDiagnostic()>;
  if constexpr (std::is_same_v<Arg, EmitFn>) {
    return [=](Rest &&...rest) {
      RaisingScopedEmitFn emitFn;
      return std::invoke(f, emitFn, std::forward<Rest>(rest)...);
    };
  } else {
    return [=](Arg &&arg, Rest &&...rest) {
      return checked([=](Rest &&...rest) {
        return std::invoke(f, std::forward<Arg>(arg),
                           std::forward<Rest>(rest)...);
      })(std::forward<Rest>(rest)...);
    };
  }
}

/// Base case for `checked` recursion
template <typename T>
constexpr auto checked(T (*f)()) {
  return f;
}

/// Wrap a `getChecked` call with a diagnostic handler which will raise a
/// python TypeError with the emitted error message.
template <typename T, typename... Args>
auto get_checked(Args &&...args) {
  using EmitFn = llvm::function_ref<mlir::InFlightDiagnostic()>;
  using Concrete =
      decltype(T::getChecked(std::declval<EmitFn>(), std::declval<Args>()...));
  using Overload = Concrete (*)(EmitFn, Args...);
  Overload getChecked = &T::getChecked;
  return checked(getChecked)(std::forward<Args>(args)...);
}

} // namespace M::Graph::Python

#endif // SDK_GRAPHAPI_PYTHON_CHECKED_H

ParseResult parseShapeParam(AsmParser &p, MOSH::ShapeAttr &shapeAttr) {
  TypedAttr attr;
  OptionalParseResult res = MOSH::parseShapeAttr(p, attr);
  if (res.has_value() && succeeded(res.value())) {
    shapeAttr = cast<MOSH::ShapeAttr>(attr);
    return success();
  }
  return p.emitError(p.getCurrentLocation())
         << "couldn't parse shape parameter: expected literal shape "
            "reference (i.e. `[...]`)";
}

class TensorLikeTypeParser {
public:
  TensorLikeTypeParser(AsmParser &parser) : parser{parser} {}

  ParseResult parse();

  template <typename TensorLikeType>
  TensorLikeType getType() {
    mlir::MLIRContext *ctx = parser.getContext();

    if (!metadata)
      metadata = mlir::DictionaryAttr::get(ctx);

    return parser.getChecked<TensorLikeType>(startLoc, ctx, shape, dtype,
                                             deviceRef, metadata);
  }

private:
  /// Parse the optional deviceRef and metadata fields.
  ParseResult parseOptionalFields();

  /// Try to parse the current token as the metadata field.
  ParseResult parseMetadata();

  /// Parse the closing '>'.
  ParseResult parseComplete();

private:
  AsmParser &parser;
  mlir::SMLoc startLoc;

  MOSH::ShapeAttr shape;
  DType dtype;
  DeviceRefAttr deviceRef;
  mlir::DictionaryAttr metadata;
};

ParseResult TensorLikeTypeParser::parseComplete() {
  return parser.parseGreater();
}

ParseResult TensorLikeTypeParser::parseMetadata() {
  // Metadata is the last field.
  if (parser.parseAttribute(metadata))
    return failure();

  // A trailing comma means the fields are out of order.
  if (parser.parseOptionalComma())
    return parseComplete();

  parser.emitError(
      parser.getCurrentLocation(),
      "attribute field order should be device followed by metadata");
  return failure();
}

ParseResult TensorLikeTypeParser::parseOptionalFields() {
  if (parser.parseOptionalComma()) {
    // An omitted device defaults to host.
    deviceRef = DeviceRefAttr::getDefault(parser.getContext());
    return parseComplete();
  }

  StringRef deviceLabel;

  // No device keyword, so the field is metadata.
  if (parser.parseOptionalKeyword(&deviceLabel)) {
    // An omitted device defaults to host.
    deviceRef = DeviceRefAttr::getDefault(parser.getContext());
    return parseMetadata();
  }

  DeviceId deviceId;

  if (parser.parseColon() || parser.parseInteger(deviceId))
    return failure();

  deviceRef = DeviceRefAttr::get(parser.getContext(), deviceLabel, deviceId);

  if (parser.parseOptionalComma())
    return parseComplete();

  return parseMetadata();
}

ParseResult TensorLikeTypeParser::parse() {
  startLoc = parser.getCurrentLocation();

  if (parser.parseLess())
    return failure();

  if (parseShapeParam(parser, shape))
    return failure();

  if (parser.parseComma())
    return failure();

  FailureOr<DType> dtypeOr = mlir::FieldParser<DType>::parse(parser);
  if (failed(dtypeOr)) {
    return parser.emitError(parser.getCurrentLocation(),
                            "invalid dtype in MO::TensorType");
  }

  dtype = dtypeOr.value();

  return parseOptionalFields();
}

void printTensorLikeType(AsmPrinter &printer, TypedAttr shape, DType dtype,
                         DeviceRefAttr device, mlir::DictionaryAttr metadata) {
  printer << '<';
  MOSH::printShapeTypedAttr(printer, shape);
  printer << ", " << dtype.getAsString();

  if (device && device != DeviceRefAttr::getDefault(device.getContext()))
    printer << ", " << device.getLabel() << ":" << device.getId();
  else if (!device)
    printer << ", INVALID_STATE_NO_DEVICE";

  if (!metadata.empty())
    printer << ", " << metadata;

  printer << '>';
}

} // end namespace

FailureOr<DType> mlir::FieldParser<DType>::parse(AsmParser &parser) {
  StringRef value;
  if (parser.parseKeyword(&value))
    return failure();
  return DType::getFromString(value);
}

static std::string asString(Type type) {
  std::string str;
  llvm::raw_string_ostream os(str);
  os << type;
  return str;
}

// TensorType
//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//

/// `MO::TensorType` metadata keys.
static constexpr StringRef kLayoutMetadataName = "layout";
static constexpr StringRef kIOKindMetadataName = "io";
static constexpr StringRef kIsMutableMetadataName = "mut";

/// A stable tensor carries a `UnitAttr` under this key in the metadata
/// `DictionaryAttr` of `MO::TensorType`.
static constexpr StringRef kIsStableMetadataName = "stable";

Type TensorType::parse(AsmParser &parser) {
  TensorLikeTypeParser tensorParser(parser);

  if (tensorParser.parse())
    return {};

  return tensorParser.getType<TensorType>();
}

void TensorType::print(AsmPrinter &printer) const {
  printTensorLikeType(printer, getShape(), getDtype(), getDeviceRef(),
                      getMetadata());
}

/// Verifies that the given dimensions represent a valid tensor shape, and
/// that the element type in DType form is also representable as an MLIR type.
LogicalResult TensorType::verify(function_ref<InFlightDiagnostic()> emitError,
                                 MOSH::ShapeAttr shape, DType dtype,
                                 DeviceRefAttr deviceRef,
                                 DictionaryAttr metadata) {
  if (!deviceRef)
    return emitError() << "no device attribute was defined";

  if (!llvm::all_of(shape.getValues(), ShapeAttr::isDim))
    return emitError() << "tensor dimensions must be a getDimType()";

  for (TypedAttr dimAttr : shape.getValues()) {
    if (auto dimInt = ShapeAttr::getStaticDim(dimAttr)) {
      if (*dimInt < 0)
        return emitError()
               << "invalid dimension, expect all dimensions >= 0 got: "
               << *dimInt;
    }
  }

  // Reject the legacy format that kept the device in metadata.
  if (metadata && metadata.contains("device"))
    return emitError()
           << "device attribute no longer resides in the metadata dictionary";

  return success();
}

// TODO: Copied from MGP; align the two.
ErrorOr<DType> M::MO::fromMLIRType(Type mlirType) {
  if (auto unkType = llvm::dyn_cast<NoneType>(mlirType))
    return DType(); // invalid denotes unknown.
  if (auto intType = llvm::dyn_cast<IntegerType>(mlirType)) {
    FailureOr<DType> dtype = getEquivalentDType(intType);
    if (succeeded(dtype) && !(dtype->isInvalid()))
      return *dtype;
  }
  if (auto floatType = llvm::dyn_cast<FloatType>(mlirType)) {
    FailureOr<DType> dtype = getEquivalentDType(floatType);
    if (succeeded(dtype) && !(dtype->isInvalid()))
      return *dtype;
  }
  return Error(Twine("unable to represent MLIR Type '") + asString(mlirType) +
               "' as an M::DType type.");
}

ErrorOr<Type> M::MO::toMLIRType(MLIRContext *context, DType dType) {
  if (!dType.isValid())
    return NoneType::get(context); // None denotes unknown.
  if (dType.isInt() || dType.isBool())
    if (Type type = getEquivalentIntegerType(context, dType))
      return type;
  if (dType.isFloat())
    if (Type type = getEquivalentFloatType(context, dType))
      return type;
  return Error(Twine("unable to represent DType '") + dType.getAsString() +
               "' as an MLIR type.");
}

DType M::MO::getDTypeOrInvalid(Type ty) {
  if (auto tensorTy = dyn_cast<TensorType>(ty))
    return tensorTy.getDtype();
  else if (auto bufferTy = dyn_cast<BufferType>(ty))
    return bufferTy.getDtype();
  ErrorOr<DType> errOr = fromMLIRType(ty);
  return errOr.isError() ? DType::invalid : *errOr;
}

TypedAttr M::MO::getShape(Type ty) {
  if (auto tensorTy = dyn_cast<TensorType>(ty))
    return tensorTy.getShape();
  else if (auto bufferTy = dyn_cast<BufferType>(ty))
    return bufferTy.getShape();

  llvm_unreachable(
      "M::MO::getShape can only take MO::BufferType or MO::TensorType");
}

// Base builder which all others call
TensorType TensorType::get(::mlir::MLIRContext *context,
                           MOSH::ShapeAttr shapeAttr, DType dtype,
                           DeviceRefAttr deviceRef, DictionaryAttr metadata) {
  if (!deviceRef)
    deviceRef = DeviceRefAttr::getDefault(context);

  return Base::get(context, std::move(shapeAttr), std::move(dtype),
                   std::move(deviceRef), std::move(metadata));
}

TensorType TensorType::getChecked(function_ref<InFlightDiagnostic()> emitError,
                                  ::mlir::MLIRContext *context,
                                  MOSH::ShapeAttr shapeAttr, DType dtype,
                                  DeviceRefAttr deviceRef,
                                  DictionaryAttr metadata) {
  if (failed(verify(emitError, shapeAttr, dtype, deviceRef, metadata)))
    return {};
  return TensorType::get(context, shapeAttr, dtype, deviceRef, metadata);
}

TensorType TensorType::get(MOSH::ShapeAttr shapeAttr, DType dtype,
                           DeviceRefAttr deviceRef, DictionaryAttr metadata) {
  MLIRContext *ctx = shapeAttr.getContext();
  if (!metadata)
    metadata = DictionaryAttr::get(ctx);
  return get(ctx, shapeAttr, dtype, deviceRef, metadata);
}

TensorType TensorType::getChecked(function_ref<InFlightDiagnostic()> emitError,
                                  MOSH::ShapeAttr shapeAttr, DType dtype,
                                  DeviceRefAttr deviceRef,
                                  DictionaryAttr metadata) {
  if (failed(verify(emitError, shapeAttr, dtype, deviceRef, metadata)))
    return {};
  return TensorType::get(shapeAttr, dtype, deviceRef, metadata);
}

TensorType TensorType::get(MOSH::ShapeAttr shapeAttr, Type elementType,
                           DeviceRefAttr deviceRef, DictionaryAttr metadata) {
  ErrorOr<DType> errOrDType = fromMLIRType(elementType);
  ASSERT_STREAM(!errOrDType.isError(),
                << "element type is not representable as a DType: "
                << errOrDType.takeError());
  return get(shapeAttr, *errOrDType, deviceRef, metadata);
}

TensorType TensorType::getChecked(function_ref<InFlightDiagnostic()> emitError,
                                  MOSH::ShapeAttr shapeAttr, Type elementType,
                                  DeviceRefAttr deviceRef,
                                  DictionaryAttr metadata) {
  ErrorOr<DType> dtype = fromMLIRType(elementType);
  if (!dtype) {
    emitError() << dtype.takeError();
    return {};
  }
  if (failed(verify(emitError, shapeAttr, *dtype, deviceRef, metadata)))
    return {};
  return TensorType::get(shapeAttr, *dtype, deviceRef, metadata);
}

TensorType TensorType::get(ArrayRef<int64_t> shape, Type elementType,
                           DeviceRefAttr deviceRef, DictionaryAttr metadata) {
  auto ctx = elementType.getContext();
  auto newShape = ShapeAttr::get(shape, ShapeType::get(ctx));
  return get(newShape, elementType, deviceRef, metadata);
}

TensorType TensorType::getChecked(function_ref<InFlightDiagnostic()> emitError,
                                  ArrayRef<int64_t> shape, Type elementType,
                                  DeviceRefAttr deviceRef,
                                  DictionaryAttr metadata) {
  auto ctx = elementType.getContext();
  auto shapeAttr = ShapeAttr::getChecked(emitError, shape, ShapeType::get(ctx));
  if (!shapeAttr)
    return {};
  return TensorType::getChecked(emitError, shapeAttr, elementType, deviceRef,
                                metadata);
}

// TODO: Delete this method.
TensorType TensorType::cloneWith(ArrayRef<int64_t> shape, Type dtype) const {
  auto shapeTy = ShapeType::get(getContext());
  auto shapeAttr = ShapeAttr::get(shape, shapeTy);

  ErrorOr<DType> errOrDType = fromMLIRType(dtype);
  ASSERT_STREAM(!errOrDType.isError(),
                << "element type is not representable as an M::DType: "
                << errOrDType.takeError());

  return TensorType::get(shapeAttr, getDtype(), getDeviceRef(), getMetadata());

TensorType TensorType::cloneWithStable(bool isStable) const {
  NamedAttrList namedAttrs(getMetadata());

  if (isStable)
    namedAttrs.set(kIsStableMetadataName, UnitAttr::get(getContext()));
  else
    namedAttrs.erase(kIsStableMetadataName);

  DictionaryAttr newMetadata = namedAttrs.getDictionary(getContext());
  return TensorType::get(getShape(), getDtype(), getDeviceRef(), newMetadata);
}

bool TensorType::isStable() const {
  return getMetadata().contains(kIsStableMetadataName);

TensorType TensorType::cloneWith(DictionaryAttr metadataAttr) const {

TensorType TensorType::cloneWith(DeviceRefAttr deviceRef) const {

bool TensorType::hasRank() const {
  // verify guarantees a ShapeAttr, which is always ranked. Kept for parity
  // with ShapedTypeInterface.
  return true;
}

size_t TensorType::getRank() const { return getShape().getRank(); }

size_t TensorType::getRankNonZero() const {
  return std::max<size_t>(1, getRank());
}

bool TensorType::hasStaticShape() const {
  return hasRank() && getShape().isStatic();
}

Type TensorType::getElementType() const {
  ErrorOr<Type> errOrType = toMLIRType(getContext(), getDtype());
  ASSERT_STREAM(!errOrType.isError(),
                << "element type is not representable as an mlir Type: "
                << errOrType.takeError());
  return *errOrType;
}

SmallPtrSet<StringAttr, 4> TensorType::getUsedParamNames() const {
  SmallPtrSet<StringAttr, 4> res;
  mlir::AttrTypeWalker walker;
  walker.addWalk(
      [&](KGEN::ParamDeclRefAttr attr) { res.insert(attr.getName()); });
  walker.walk(getShape());
  return res;
}

ArrayRef<TypedAttr> TensorType::getDims() const {
  return getShape().getValues();
}

TypedAttr TensorType::getDim(size_t n) const { return getDims()[n]; }

bool TensorType::isParameterizedDim(size_t n) const {
  return isParameterizedDimParam(getDim(n));
}

bool TensorType::isIntegerDim(size_t n) const {
  return isIntegerDimParam(getDim(n));
}

bool TensorType::isParameterizedDimParam(TypedAttr attr) {
  bool isParamOrParamExpr = llvm::isa<KGEN::ParamDeclRefAttr>(attr) ||
                            llvm::isa<KGEN::ParamOperatorAttr>(attr);
  return isParamOrParamExpr && ShapeAttr::isDim(attr);
}

bool TensorType::isIntegerDimParam(TypedAttr attr) {
  return ShapeAttr::getStaticDim(attr).has_value();
}

SmallVector<int64_t> TensorType::getIntDims() const {
  return getShape().getIntDims();
}

int64_t TensorType::getIntDim(size_t n) const {
  return getShape().getIntDim(n);
}

TypedAttr TensorType::getSymbolicNumElements() const {
  return getShape().getSymbolicNumElements();
}

std::optional<int64_t> TensorType::getNumElements() const {
  if (!hasRank())
    return {};

  TypedAttr attr = getSymbolicNumElements();
  auto numElements = ShapeAttr::getStaticDim(attr);
  if (!numElements.has_value())
    return {};

  // We allow one -1 dimension for now, which is a fancy parameter.
  // TODO(15523): maybe remove once -1 is handled more gracefully.
  if (*numElements < 0)
    return {};

  return *numElements;
}

TensorType TensorType::cloneWithNewDim(uint64_t dim, uint64_t size) {
  SmallVector<TypedAttr> shape(getDims());
  shape[dim] = ShapeAttr::getDim(shape.front().getContext(), size);
  auto shapeAttr = ShapeAttr::get(shape, ShapeType::get(getContext()));

  return cloneWith(shapeAttr);
}

//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
// ListType
//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//

LogicalResult ListType::verify(function_ref<InFlightDiagnostic()> emitError,
                               Type elementType) {
  // check against things like `!mo.list<f32>`
  auto tensorTy = llvm::dyn_cast<TensorType>(elementType);
  if (!tensorTy) {
    return emitError() << "list can only contain tensor elements, but got "
                       << elementType;
  }

  // check against things like `!mo.list<!mo.tensor<[20, D0], f32>>`
  for (TypedAttr dimAttr : tensorTy.getShape().getValues()) {
    if (llvm::isa<KGEN::ParamDeclRefAttr>(dimAttr))
      return emitError() << "tensor element dimensions cannot have parameter";
  }

  return success();
}

DeviceRefAttr ListType::getDeviceRef() const {
  auto tensorType = llvm::cast<TensorType>(getElementType());
  return tensorType.getDeviceRef();
}

Type ListType::cloneWithNewDevice(DeviceRefAttr device) const {
  auto tensorType = llvm::cast<TensorType>(getElementType());
  return ListType::get(getContext(), tensorType.cloneWithNewDevice(device));
}

//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
// BundleType
//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//

namespace {

/// A bundle whose element tensor types are reconstructible from one
/// shape/dtype/device-range tuple; the compact form shared by the BundleType
/// printer and parser.
struct CompactBundleInfo {
  TypedAttr shapeAttr;
  DType dtype;
  // Non-null.
  DeviceRefAttr deviceRef;
  DictionaryAttr metadata;
  // IDs of elements 0 and N-1.
  DeviceId firstId;
  DeviceId lastId;
};

/// Returns a CompactBundleInfo iff all elements are TensorTypes with identical
/// shape, dtype, device label, and metadata, and contiguous device IDs
/// (`ids[i] == ids[0] + i`).
std::optional<CompactBundleInfo>
computeCompactBundleInfo(ArrayRef<Type> elementTypes) {
  if (elementTypes.empty())
    return std::nullopt;

  auto first = llvm::dyn_cast<TensorType>(elementTypes.front());
  if (!first)
    return std::nullopt;

  DeviceRefAttr firstDevice = first.getDeviceRef();
  if (!firstDevice)
    return std::nullopt;

  DeviceId firstId = firstDevice.getId();
  for (auto [idx, ty] : llvm::enumerate(elementTypes)) {
    auto tensor = llvm::dyn_cast<TensorType>(ty);
    if (!tensor)
      return std::nullopt;
    if (tensor.getShape() != first.getShape())
      return std::nullopt;
    if (tensor.getDtype() != first.getDtype())
      return std::nullopt;
    if (tensor.getMetadata() != first.getMetadata())
      return std::nullopt;
    DeviceRefAttr devRef = tensor.getDeviceRef();
    if (!devRef || devRef.getLabel() != firstDevice.getLabel())
      return std::nullopt;
    if (devRef.getId() != firstId + static_cast<DeviceId>(idx))
      return std::nullopt;
  }

  DeviceId lastId = firstId + static_cast<DeviceId>(elementTypes.size() - 1);
  return CompactBundleInfo{first.getShape(),    first.getDtype(), firstDevice,
                           first.getMetadata(), firstId,          lastId};
}

} // namespace

Type BundleType::parse(AsmParser &parser) {
  if (parser.parseLess() || parser.parseLSquare())
    return {};

  // The verbose form has a tensor type here; the compact form has shape dims,
  // which are not a type.
  Type firstType;
  OptionalParseResult typeRes = parser.parseOptionalType(firstType);
  if (typeRes.has_value()) {
    if (failed(*typeRes))
      return {};

    // Verbose form.
    SmallVector<Type> elementTypes{firstType};
    while (succeeded(parser.parseOptionalComma())) {
      Type ty;
      if (parser.parseType(ty))
        return {};
      elementTypes.push_back(ty);
    }
    if (parser.parseRSquare() || parser.parseGreater())
      return {};
    return BundleType::get(parser.getContext(), elementTypes);
  }

  // Compact form; the outer `[` doubles as the shape's bracket.
  MLIRContext *ctx = parser.getContext();
  auto shapeTy = parser.getBuilder().getType<ShapeType>();
  SmallVector<TypedAttr> shapeDims;
  if (MOSH::parseShapeValue(parser, shapeDims) || parser.parseRSquare())
    return {};
  auto shapeAttr = parser.getChecked<ShapeAttr>(shapeDims, shapeTy);
  if (!shapeAttr)
    return {};

  if (parser.parseComma())
    return {};

  FailureOr<DType> dtypeOr = mlir::FieldParser<DType>::parse(parser);
  if (failed(dtypeOr))
    return {};
  DType dtype = dtypeOr.value();

  // Optional device section: `, <label>:<id>[-<lastId>]`.
  DeviceRefAttr firstDevice;
  DeviceId firstId = 0;
  DeviceId lastId = 0;
  bool hasExplicitDevice = false;
  DictionaryAttr metadata;

  if (succeeded(parser.parseOptionalComma())) {
    StringRef deviceLabel;
    if (succeeded(parser.parseOptionalKeyword(&deviceLabel))) {
      hasExplicitDevice = true;
      if (parser.parseColon() || parser.parseInteger(firstId))
        return {};
      lastId = firstId;

      // AsmParser has no parseMinus, but the lexer tokenizes `-3` as one
      // signed integer whose absolute value is the range end.
      int64_t rangeEnd = 0;
      OptionalParseResult rangeRes = parser.parseOptionalInteger(rangeEnd);
      if (rangeRes.has_value()) {
        if (failed(*rangeRes))
          return {};
        if (rangeEnd >= 0) {
          parser.emitError(parser.getCurrentLocation())
              << "expected '-' before compact bundle device range end";
          return {};
        }
        lastId = static_cast<DeviceId>(-rangeEnd);
        if (lastId < firstId) {
          parser.emitError(parser.getCurrentLocation())
              << "compact bundle device range must be ordered "
              << "(firstId <= lastId)";
          return {};
        }
      }

      firstDevice = DeviceRefAttr::get(ctx, deviceLabel, firstId);

      if (succeeded(parser.parseOptionalComma())) {
        if (parser.parseAttribute(metadata))
          return {};
      }
    } else {
      if (parser.parseAttribute(metadata))
        return {};
    }
  }

  if (parser.parseGreater())
    return {};

  if (!hasExplicitDevice)
    firstDevice = DeviceRefAttr::getDefault(ctx);
  if (!metadata)
    metadata = DictionaryAttr::get(ctx);

  size_t numElements =
      hasExplicitDevice ? static_cast<size_t>(lastId - firstId + 1) : 1;
  SmallVector<Type> elementTypes;
  elementTypes.reserve(numElements);
  for (size_t i = 0; i < numElements; ++i) {
    DeviceRefAttr devRef =
        hasExplicitDevice
            ? DeviceRefAttr::get(ctx, firstDevice.getLabel(), firstId + i)
            : firstDevice;
    auto tensor =
        parser.getChecked<TensorType>(ctx, shapeAttr, dtype, devRef, metadata);
    if (!tensor)
      return {};
    elementTypes.push_back(tensor);
  }
  return BundleType::get(ctx, elementTypes);
}

void BundleType::print(AsmPrinter &printer) const {
  ArrayRef<Type> elementTypes = getElementTypes();

  if (auto info = computeCompactBundleInfo(elementTypes)) {
    printer << '<';
    MOSH::printShapeTypedAttr(printer, info->shapeAttr);
    printer << ", " << info->dtype.getAsString();

    // Elide the device only when the parser would re-derive it: a single
    // element on the default host device.
    auto defaultDev = DeviceRefAttr::getDefault(getContext());
    bool singleDefault =
        elementTypes.size() == 1 && info->deviceRef == defaultDev;
    if (!singleDefault) {
      printer << ", " << info->deviceRef.getLabel() << ':' << info->firstId;
      if (info->firstId != info->lastId)
        printer << '-' << info->lastId;
    }

    if (info->metadata && !info->metadata.empty())
      printer << ", " << info->metadata;

    printer << '>';
    return;
  }

  printer << "<[";
  llvm::interleaveComma(elementTypes, printer,
                        [&](Type ty) { printer.printType(ty); });
  printer << "]>";
}

LogicalResult BundleType::verify(function_ref<InFlightDiagnostic()> emitError,
                                 ArrayRef<Type> elementTypes) {
  if (elementTypes.empty())
    return emitError() << "bundle must have at least one element";
  bool allTensors = llvm::all_of(
      elementTypes, [](Type t) { return llvm::isa<TensorType>(t); });
  if (!allTensors)
    return emitError() << "bundle elements must all be !mo.tensor types";
  return success();
}

//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
// Device list printing / parsing
//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//

namespace M::MO {

void printDeviceList(AsmPrinter &printer, ArrayRef<DeviceRefAttr> devices) {
  if (devices.empty())
    return;

  // Compact `label:first[-last]` form when labels match and IDs are
  // consecutive.
  StringRef label = devices.front().getLabel();
  DeviceId firstId = devices.front().getId();
  bool isContiguous = true;
  for (auto [i, d] : llvm::enumerate(devices)) {
    if (d.getLabel() != label ||
        d.getId() != firstId + static_cast<DeviceId>(i)) {
      isContiguous = false;
      break;
    }
  }
  if (isContiguous) {
    printer << label << ':' << firstId;
    if (devices.size() > 1)
      printer << '-' << (firstId + devices.size() - 1);
    return;
  }

  llvm::interleaveComma(devices, printer, [&](DeviceRefAttr d) {
    printer << d.getLabel() << ':' << d.getId();
  });
}

ParseResult parseDeviceList(AsmParser &parser,
                            SmallVectorImpl<DeviceRefAttr> &devices) {
  MLIRContext *ctx = parser.getContext();

  // Entries are `label:id` or `label:id-lastId` and may mix, e.g.
  // `gpu:0-3, cpu:0`.
  auto parseOneEntry = [&]() -> ParseResult {
    StringRef label;
    if (parser.parseKeyword(&label))
      return failure();
    DeviceId firstId = 0;
    if (parser.parseColon() || parser.parseInteger(firstId))
      return failure();
    DeviceId lastId = firstId;

    // The lexer tokenizes `-<lastId>` as one signed integer.
    int64_t rangeEnd = 0;
    OptionalParseResult rangeRes = parser.parseOptionalInteger(rangeEnd);
    if (rangeRes.has_value()) {
      if (failed(*rangeRes))
        return failure();
      if (rangeEnd >= 0)
        return parser.emitError(parser.getCurrentLocation(),
                                "expected '-' before compact device range end");
      lastId = static_cast<DeviceId>(-rangeEnd);
      if (lastId < firstId)
        return parser.emitError(
            parser.getCurrentLocation(),
            "compact device range must be ordered (firstId <= lastId)");
    }

    for (DeviceId id = firstId; id <= lastId; ++id)
      devices.push_back(DeviceRefAttr::get(ctx, label, id));
    return success();
  };

  if (parseOneEntry())
    return failure();
  while (succeeded(parser.parseOptionalComma())) {
    if (parseOneEntry())
      return failure();
  }
  return success();
}

} // namespace M::MO

BufferType BufferType::cloneWith(DeviceRefAttr deviceRef) const {
  return BufferType::get(getContext(), getShape(), getDtype(), deviceRef,
                         getMetadata());
}

Type BufferType::parse(AsmParser &parser) {
  TensorLikeTypeParser bufferParser(parser);

  if (bufferParser.parse())
    return {};

  return bufferParser.getType<BufferType>();
}

void BufferType::print(AsmPrinter &printer) const {
  printTensorLikeType(printer, getShape(), getDtype(), getDeviceRef(),
                      getMetadata());
}

/// Verifies that the given dimensions represent a valid tensor shape, and
/// that the element type in DType form is also representable as an MLIR type.
LogicalResult BufferType::verify(function_ref<InFlightDiagnostic()> emitError,
                                 MOSH::ShapeAttr shape, DType dtype,
                                 DeviceRefAttr deviceRef,
                                 DictionaryAttr metadata) {
  if (!deviceRef)
    return emitError() << "no device attribute was defined";

  for (TypedAttr dimAttr : shape.getValues()) {
    if (auto dimInt = ShapeAttr::getStaticDim(dimAttr)) {
      if (*dimInt < 0)
        return emitError()
               << "invalid dimension, expect all dimensions >= 0 got: "
               << *dimInt;
    }
  }

  if (!llvm::all_of(shape.getValues(), ShapeAttr::isDim))
    return emitError() << "buffer dimensions must be a getDimType()";

  // Reject the legacy format that kept the device in metadata.
  if (metadata && metadata.contains("device"))
    return emitError()
           << "device attribute no longer resides in the metadata dictionary";

  return success();
}

// Base builder which all others call
BufferType BufferType::get(::mlir::MLIRContext *context, MOSH::ShapeAttr shape,
                           DType dtype, DeviceRefAttr deviceRef,
                           DictionaryAttr metadata) {
  if (!deviceRef)
    deviceRef = DeviceRefAttr::getDefault(context);

  return Base::get(context, std::move(shape), std::move(dtype),
                   std::move(deviceRef), std::move(metadata));
}

BufferType BufferType::getChecked(function_ref<InFlightDiagnostic()> emitError,
                                  ::mlir::MLIRContext *context,
                                  MOSH::ShapeAttr shape, DType dtype,
                                  DeviceRefAttr deviceRef,
                                  DictionaryAttr metadata) {
  if (failed(verify(emitError, shape, dtype, deviceRef, metadata)))
    return {};
  return BufferType::get(context, shape, dtype, deviceRef, metadata);
}

BufferType BufferType::get(MOSH::ShapeAttr shape, DType dtype,
                           DeviceRefAttr deviceRef, DictionaryAttr metadata) {
  MLIRContext *ctx = shape.getContext();
  if (!metadata)
    metadata = DictionaryAttr::get(ctx);
  return get(ctx, shape, dtype, deviceRef, metadata);
}

BufferType BufferType::getChecked(function_ref<InFlightDiagnostic()> emitError,
                                  MOSH::ShapeAttr shape, DType dtype,
                                  DeviceRefAttr deviceRef,
                                  DictionaryAttr metadata) {
  if (failed(verify(emitError, shape, dtype, deviceRef, metadata)))
    return {};
  return BufferType::get(shape, dtype, deviceRef, metadata);
}

BufferType BufferType::get(MOSH::ShapeAttr shape, Type elementType,
                           DeviceRefAttr deviceRef, DictionaryAttr metadata) {
  ErrorOr<DType> errOrDType = fromMLIRType(elementType);
  ASSERT_STREAM(!errOrDType.isError(),
                << "element type is not representable as a DType: "
                << errOrDType.takeError());
  return get(shape, *errOrDType, deviceRef, metadata);
}

BufferType BufferType::getChecked(function_ref<InFlightDiagnostic()> emitError,
                                  MOSH::ShapeAttr shape, Type elementType,
                                  DeviceRefAttr deviceRef,
                                  DictionaryAttr metadata) {
  ErrorOr<DType> dtype = fromMLIRType(elementType);
  if (!dtype) {
    emitError() << dtype.takeError();
    return {};
  }
  if (failed(verify(emitError, shape, *dtype, deviceRef, metadata)))
    return {};
  return BufferType::get(shape, *dtype, deviceRef, metadata);
}

BufferType BufferType::get(ArrayRef<TypedAttr> shape, Type elementType,
                           DeviceRefAttr deviceRef, DictionaryAttr metadata) {
  auto ctx = elementType.getContext();
  auto newShape = ShapeAttr::get(shape, ShapeType::get(ctx));
  return get(newShape, elementType, deviceRef, metadata);
}

BufferType BufferType::getChecked(function_ref<InFlightDiagnostic()> emitError,
                                  ArrayRef<TypedAttr> shape, Type elementType,
                                  DeviceRefAttr deviceRef,
                                  DictionaryAttr metadata) {
  auto ctx = elementType.getContext();
  auto newShape = ShapeAttr::getChecked(emitError, shape, ShapeType::get(ctx));
  if (!newShape)
    return {};
  return BufferType::getChecked(emitError, newShape, elementType, deviceRef,
                                metadata);
}

BufferType BufferType::get(TensorType tensorType) {
  return get(tensorType.getShape(), tensorType.getElementType(),
             tensorType.getDeviceRef(), tensorType.getMetadata());
}

BufferType BufferType::getChecked(function_ref<InFlightDiagnostic()> emitError,
                                  TensorType tensorType) {
  if (failed(verify(emitError, tensorType.getShape(), tensorType.getDtype(),
                    tensorType.getDeviceRef(), tensorType.getMetadata())))
    return {};
  return BufferType::get(tensorType);
}

TensorType BufferType::toTensorType(BufferType ty) {
  auto shape = ty.getShape();
  auto dtype = ty.getDtype();
  auto deviceRef = ty.getDeviceRef();
  auto metadata = ty.getMetadata();

  return TensorType::get(shape, dtype, deviceRef, metadata);
}

TensorType BufferType::toTensorType() {
  return BufferType::toTensorType(*this);
}

TensorType M::MO::castFromTensorLike(Type ty) {
  if (auto tensorTy = dyn_cast<TensorType>(ty))
    return tensorTy;
  return BufferType::toTensorType(cast<MO::BufferType>(ty));
}

TensorType M::MO::dynCastFromTensorLike(Type ty) {
  if (auto tensorTy = dyn_cast<TensorType>(ty))
    return tensorTy;
  if (auto bufferTy = dyn_cast<BufferType>(ty))
    return BufferType::toTensorType(bufferTy);
  return nullptr;
}

size_t BufferType::getRank() const { return getShape().getRank(); }

size_t BufferType::getRankNonZero() const {
  size_t rank = getRank();
  return rank == 0 ? rank + 1 : rank;
}

/// Helper class for implementing traits for storage classes. Clients are not
/// expected to interact with this directly, so its members are all protected.
template <typename ConcreteType, template <typename> class TraitType>
class StorageUserTraitBase {
protected:
  /// Return the derived instance.
  ConcreteType getInstance() const {
    // We have to cast up to the trait type, then to the concrete type because
    // the concrete type will multiply derive from the (content free) TraitBase
    // class, and we need to be able to disambiguate the path for the C++
    // compiler.
    auto *trait = static_cast<const TraitType<ConcreteType> *>(this);
    return *static_cast<const ConcreteType *>(trait);
  }
};

namespace StorageUserTrait {
/// This trait is used to determine if a storage user, like Type, is mutable
/// or not. A storage user is mutable if ImplType of the derived class defines
/// a `mutate` function with a proper signature. Note that this trait is not
/// supposed to be used publicly. Users should use alias names like
/// `TypeTrait::IsMutable` instead.
template <typename ConcreteType>
struct IsMutable : public StorageUserTraitBase<ConcreteType, IsMutable> {};
} // namespace StorageUserTrait

//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
// StorageUserBase
//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//

namespace storage_user_base_impl {
/// Returns true if this given Trait ID matches the IDs of any of the provided
/// trait types `Traits`.
template <template <typename T> class... Traits>
bool hasTrait(TypeID traitID) {
  TypeID traitIDs[] = {TypeID::get<Traits>()...};
  for (unsigned i = 0, e = sizeof...(Traits); i != e; ++i)
    if (traitIDs[i] == traitID)
      return true;
  return false;
}

// We specialize for the empty case to not define an empty array.
template <>
inline bool hasTrait(TypeID traitID) {
  return false;
}
} // namespace storage_user_base_impl

/// Utility class for implementing users of storage classes uniqued by a
/// StorageUniquer. Clients are not expected to interact with this class
/// directly.
template <typename ConcreteT, typename BaseT, typename StorageT,
          typename UniquerT, template <typename T> class... Traits>
class StorageUserBase : public BaseT, public Traits<ConcreteT>... {
public:
  using BaseT::BaseT;

  /// Utility declarations for the concrete attribute class.
  using Base = StorageUserBase<ConcreteT, BaseT, StorageT, UniquerT, Traits...>;
  using ImplType = StorageT;
  using HasTraitFn = bool (*)(TypeID);

  /// Return a unique identifier for the concrete type.
  static TypeID getTypeID() { return TypeID::get<ConcreteT>(); }

  /// Provide an implementation of 'classof' that compares the type id of the
  /// provided value with that of the concrete type.
  template <typename T>
  static bool classof(T val) {
    static_assert(std::is_convertible<ConcreteT, T>::value,
                  "casting from a non-convertible type");
    return val.getTypeID() == getTypeID();
  }

  /// Returns an interface map for the interfaces registered to this storage
  /// user. This should not be used directly.
  static detail::InterfaceMap getInterfaceMap() {
    return detail::InterfaceMap::template get<Traits<ConcreteT>...>();
  }

  /// Returns the function that returns true if the given Trait ID matches the
  /// IDs of any of the traits defined by the storage user.
  static HasTraitFn getHasTraitFn() {
    return [](TypeID id) {
      return storage_user_base_impl::hasTrait<Traits...>(id);
    };
  }

  /// Returns a function that walks immediate sub elements of a given instance
  /// of the storage user.
  static auto getWalkImmediateSubElementsFn() {
    return [](auto instance, function_ref<void(Attribute)> walkAttrsFn,
              function_ref<void(Type)> walkTypesFn) {
      ::mlir::detail::walkImmediateSubElementsImpl(
          llvm::cast<ConcreteT>(instance), walkAttrsFn, walkTypesFn);
    };
  }

  /// Returns a function that replaces immediate sub elements of a given
  /// instance of the storage user.
  static auto getReplaceImmediateSubElementsFn() {
    return [](auto instance, ArrayRef<Attribute> replAttrs,
              ArrayRef<Type> replTypes) {
      return ::mlir::detail::replaceImmediateSubElementsImpl(
          llvm::cast<ConcreteT>(instance), replAttrs, replTypes);
    };
  }

  /// Attach the given models as implementations of the corresponding interfaces
  /// for the concrete storage user class. The type must be registered with the
  /// context, i.e. the dialect to which the type belongs must be loaded. The
  /// call will abort otherwise.
  template <typename... IfaceModels>
  static void attachInterface(MLIRContext &context) {
    typename ConcreteT::AbstractTy *abstract =
        ConcreteT::AbstractTy::lookupMutable(TypeID::get<ConcreteT>(),
                                             &context);
    if (!abstract)
      llvm::report_fatal_error("Registering an interface for an attribute/type "
                               "that is not itself registered.");

    // Handle the case where the models resolve a promised interface.
    (dialect_extension_detail::handleAdditionOfUndefinedPromisedInterface(
         abstract->getDialect(), abstract->getTypeID(),
         IfaceModels::Interface::getInterfaceID()),
     ...);

    (checkInterfaceTarget<IfaceModels>(), ...);
    abstract->interfaceMap.template insertModels<IfaceModels...>();
  }

  /// Get or create a new ConcreteT instance within the ctx. This
  /// function is guaranteed to return a non null object and will assert if
  /// the arguments provided are invalid.
  template <typename... Args>
  static ConcreteT get(MLIRContext *ctx, Args &&...args) {
    // Ensure that the invariants are correct for construction.
    assert(succeeded(
        ConcreteT::verifyInvariants(getDefaultDiagnosticEmitFn(ctx), args...)));
    return UniquerT::template get<ConcreteT>(ctx, std::forward<Args>(args)...);
  }

  /// Get or create a new ConcreteT instance within the ctx, defined at
  /// the given, potentially unknown, location. If the arguments provided are
  /// invalid, errors are emitted using the provided location and a null object
  /// is returned.
  template <typename... Args>
  static ConcreteT getChecked(const Location &loc, Args &&...args) {
    return ConcreteT::getChecked(getDefaultDiagnosticEmitFn(loc),
                                 std::forward<Args>(args)...);
  }

  /// Get or create a new ConcreteT instance within the ctx. If the arguments
  /// provided are invalid, errors are emitted using the provided `emitError`
  /// and a null object is returned.
  ///
  /// Workaround: We use Arg1 && instead of MLIRContext * in the parameter list
  /// to work around a bug in Clang 21.1.8 where Clang segfaults during SFINAE
  /// overload resolution when attempting to match non-pointer arguments
  /// against an unconstrained MLIRContext * parameter.
  template <typename Arg1, typename... Args,
            typename = std::enable_if_t<std::is_convertible_v<
                llvm::remove_cvref_t<Arg1>, MLIRContext *>>>
  static ConcreteT getChecked(function_ref<InFlightDiagnostic()> emitErrorFn,
                              Arg1 &&ctx, Args... args) {
    // If the construction invariants fail then we return a null attribute.
    if (failed(ConcreteT::verifyInvariants(emitErrorFn, args...)))
      return ConcreteT();
    return UniquerT::template get<ConcreteT>(ctx, std::forward<Args>(args)...);
  }

  /// Get an instance of the concrete type from a void pointer.
  static ConcreteT getFromOpaquePointer(const void *ptr) {
    return ConcreteT((const typename BaseT::ImplType *)ptr);
  }

  /// Utility for easy access to the storage instance.
  ImplType *getImpl() const { return static_cast<ImplType *>(this->impl); }

protected:
  /// Mutate the current storage instance. This will not change the unique key.
  /// The arguments are forwarded to 'ConcreteT::mutate'.
  template <typename... Args>
  LogicalResult mutate(Args &&...args) {
    static_assert(std::is_base_of<StorageUserTrait::IsMutable<ConcreteT>,
                                  ConcreteT>::value,
                  "The `mutate` function expects mutable trait "
                  "(e.g. TypeTrait::IsMutable) to be attached on parent.");
    return UniquerT::template mutate<ConcreteT>(this->getContext(), getImpl(),
                                                std::forward<Args>(args)...);
  }

  /// Default implementation that just returns success.
  template <typename... Args>
  static LogicalResult verifyInvariants(Args... args) {
    return success();
  }

private:
  /// Trait to check if T provides a 'ConcreteEntity' type alias.
  template <typename T>
  using has_concrete_entity_t = typename T::ConcreteEntity;

  /// A struct-wrapped type alias to T::ConcreteEntity if provided and to
  /// ConcreteT otherwise. This is akin to std::conditional but doesn't fail on
  /// the missing typedef. Useful for checking if the interface is targeting the
  /// right class.
  template <typename T,
            bool = llvm::is_detected<has_concrete_entity_t, T>::value>
  struct IfaceTargetOrConcreteT {
    using type = typename T::ConcreteEntity;
  };
  template <typename T>
  struct IfaceTargetOrConcreteT<T, false> {
    using type = ConcreteT;
  };

  /// A hook for static assertion that the external interface model T is
  /// targeting a base class of the concrete attribute/type. The model can also
  /// be a fallback model that works for every attribute/type.
  template <typename T>
  static void checkInterfaceTarget() {
    static_assert(std::is_base_of<typename IfaceTargetOrConcreteT<T>::type,
                                  ConcreteT>::value,
                  "attaching an interface to the wrong attribute/type kind");
  }
};
} // namespace detail
} // namespace mlir

#endif

#ifndef MLIR_IR_TYPESUPPORT_H
#define MLIR_IR_TYPESUPPORT_H

#include "mlir/IR/MLIRContext.h"
#include "mlir/IR/StorageUniquerSupport.h"
#include "llvm/ADT/Twine.h"

namespace mlir {
class Dialect;
class MLIRContext;

//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
// AbstractType
//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//

/// This class contains all of the static information common to all instances of
/// a registered Type.
class AbstractType {
public:
  using HasTraitFn = llvm::unique_function<bool(TypeID) const>;
  using WalkImmediateSubElementsFn = function_ref<void(
      Type, function_ref<void(Attribute)>, function_ref<void(Type)>)>;
  using ReplaceImmediateSubElementsFn =
      function_ref<Type(Type, ArrayRef<Attribute>, ArrayRef<Type>)>;

  /// Look up the specified abstract type in the MLIRContext and return a
  /// reference to it.
  static const AbstractType &lookup(TypeID typeID, MLIRContext *context);

  /// Look up the specified abstract type in the MLIRContext and return a
  /// reference to it if it exists.
  static std::optional<std::reference_wrapper<const AbstractType>>
  lookup(StringRef name, MLIRContext *context);

  /// This method is used by Dialect objects when they register the list of
  /// types they contain.
  template <typename T>
  static AbstractType get(Dialect &dialect) {
    return AbstractType(dialect, T::getInterfaceMap(), T::getHasTraitFn(),
                        T::getWalkImmediateSubElementsFn(),
                        T::getReplaceImmediateSubElementsFn(), T::getTypeID(),
                        T::name);
  }

  /// This method is used by Dialect objects to register types with
  /// custom TypeIDs.
  /// The use of this method is in general discouraged in favor of
  /// 'get<CustomType>(dialect)';
  static AbstractType
  get(Dialect &dialect, detail::InterfaceMap &&interfaceMap,
      HasTraitFn &&hasTrait,
      WalkImmediateSubElementsFn walkImmediateSubElementsFn,
      ReplaceImmediateSubElementsFn replaceImmediateSubElementsFn,
      TypeID typeID, StringRef name) {
    return AbstractType(dialect, std::move(interfaceMap), std::move(hasTrait),
                        walkImmediateSubElementsFn,
                        replaceImmediateSubElementsFn, typeID, name);
  }

  /// Return the dialect this type was registered to.
  Dialect &getDialect() const { return const_cast<Dialect &>(dialect); }

  /// Returns an instance of the concept object for the given interface if it
  /// was registered to this type, null otherwise. This should not be used
  /// directly.
  template <typename T>
  typename T::Concept *getInterface() const {
    return interfaceMap.lookup<T>();
  }

  /// Returns true if the type has the interface with the given ID.
  bool hasInterface(TypeID interfaceID) const {
    return interfaceMap.contains(interfaceID);
  }

  /// Returns true if the type has a particular trait.
  template <template <typename T> class Trait>
  bool hasTrait() const {
    return hasTraitFn(TypeID::get<Trait>());
  }

  /// Returns true if the type has a particular trait.
  bool hasTrait(TypeID traitID) const { return hasTraitFn(traitID); }

  /// Walk the immediate sub-elements of the given type.
  void walkImmediateSubElements(Type type,
                                function_ref<void(Attribute)> walkAttrsFn,
                                function_ref<void(Type)> walkTypesFn) const;

  /// Replace the immediate sub-elements of the given type.
  Type replaceImmediateSubElements(Type type, ArrayRef<Attribute> replAttrs,
                                   ArrayRef<Type> replTypes) const;

  /// Return the unique identifier representing the concrete type class.
  TypeID getTypeID() const { return typeID; }

  /// Return the unique name representing the type.
  StringRef getName() const { return name; }

private:
  AbstractType(Dialect &dialect, detail::InterfaceMap &&interfaceMap,
               HasTraitFn &&hasTrait,
               WalkImmediateSubElementsFn walkImmediateSubElementsFn,
               ReplaceImmediateSubElementsFn replaceImmediateSubElementsFn,
               TypeID typeID, StringRef name)
      : dialect(dialect), interfaceMap(std::move(interfaceMap)),
        hasTraitFn(std::move(hasTrait)),
        walkImmediateSubElementsFn(walkImmediateSubElementsFn),
        replaceImmediateSubElementsFn(replaceImmediateSubElementsFn),
        typeID(typeID), name(name) {}

  /// Give StorageUserBase access to the mutable lookup.
  template <typename ConcreteT, typename BaseT, typename StorageT,
            typename UniquerT, template <typename T> class... Traits>
  friend class detail::StorageUserBase;

  /// Look up the specified abstract type in the MLIRContext and return a
  /// (mutable) pointer to it. Return a null pointer if the type could not
  /// be found in the context.
  static AbstractType *lookupMutable(TypeID typeID, MLIRContext *context);

  /// This is the dialect that this type was registered to.
  const Dialect &dialect;

  /// This is a collection of the interfaces registered to this type.
  detail::InterfaceMap interfaceMap;

  /// Function to check if the type has a particular trait.
  HasTraitFn hasTraitFn;

  /// Function to walk the immediate sub-elements of this type.
  WalkImmediateSubElementsFn walkImmediateSubElementsFn;

  /// Function to replace the immediate sub-elements of this type.
  ReplaceImmediateSubElementsFn replaceImmediateSubElementsFn;

  /// The unique identifier of the derived Type class.
  const TypeID typeID;

  /// The unique name of this type. The string is not owned by the context, so
  /// The lifetime of this string should outlive the MLIR context.
  const StringRef name;
};

//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
// TypeStorage
//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//

namespace detail {
struct TypeUniquer;
} // namespace detail

/// Base storage class appearing in a Type.
class TypeStorage : public StorageUniquer::BaseStorage {
  friend detail::TypeUniquer;
  friend StorageUniquer;

public:
  /// Return the abstract type descriptor for this type.
  const AbstractType &getAbstractType() {
    assert(abstractType && "Malformed type storage object.");
    return *abstractType;
  }

protected:
  /// This constructor is used by derived classes as part of the TypeUniquer.
  TypeStorage() {}

private:
  /// Set the abstract type for this storage instance. This is used by the
  /// TypeUniquer when initializing a newly constructed type storage object.
  void initialize(const AbstractType &abstractTy) {
    abstractType = const_cast<AbstractType *>(&abstractTy);
  }

  /// The abstract description for this type.
  AbstractType *abstractType{nullptr};
};

/// Default storage type for types that require no additional initialization or
/// storage.
using DefaultTypeStorage = TypeStorage;

//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
// TypeStorageAllocator
//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//

/// This is a utility allocator used to allocate memory for instances of derived
/// Types.
using TypeStorageAllocator = StorageUniquer::StorageAllocator;

//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
// TypeUniquer
//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
namespace detail {
/// A utility class to get, or create, unique instances of types within an
/// MLIRContext. This class manages all creation and uniquing of types.
struct TypeUniquer {
  /// Get an uniqued instance of a type T.
  template <typename T, typename... Args>
  static T get(MLIRContext *ctx, Args &&...args) {
    return getWithTypeID<T, Args...>(ctx, T::getTypeID(),
                                     std::forward<Args>(args)...);
  }

  /// Get an uniqued instance of a parametric type T.
  /// The use of this method is in general discouraged in favor of
  /// 'get<T, Args>(ctx, args)'.
  template <typename T, typename... Args>
  static std::enable_if_t<
      !std::is_same<typename T::ImplType, TypeStorage>::value, T>
  getWithTypeID(MLIRContext *ctx, TypeID typeID, Args &&...args) {
#ifndef NDEBUG
    if (!ctx->getTypeUniquer().isParametricStorageInitialized(typeID))
      llvm::report_fatal_error(
          llvm::Twine("can't create type '") + llvm::getTypeName<T>() +
          "' because storage uniquer isn't initialized: the dialect was likely "
          "not loaded, or the type wasn't added with addTypes<...>() "
          "in the Dialect::initialize() method.");
#endif
    return ctx->getTypeUniquer().get<typename T::ImplType>(
        [&, typeID](TypeStorage *storage) {
          storage->initialize(AbstractType::lookup(typeID, ctx));
        },
        typeID, std::forward<Args>(args)...);
  }
  /// Get an uniqued instance of a singleton type T.
  /// The use of this method is in general discouraged in favor of
  /// 'get<T, Args>(ctx, args)'.
  template <typename T>
  static std::enable_if_t<
      std::is_same<typename T::ImplType, TypeStorage>::value, T>
  getWithTypeID(MLIRContext *ctx, TypeID typeID) {
#ifndef NDEBUG
    if (!ctx->getTypeUniquer().isSingletonStorageInitialized(typeID))
      llvm::report_fatal_error(
          llvm::Twine("can't create type '") + llvm::getTypeName<T>() +
          "' because storage uniquer isn't initialized: the dialect was likely "
          "not loaded, or the type wasn't added with addTypes<...>() "
          "in the Dialect::initialize() method.");
#endif
    return ctx->getTypeUniquer().get<typename T::ImplType>(typeID);
  }

  /// Change the mutable component of the given type instance in the provided
  /// context.
  template <typename T, typename... Args>
  static LogicalResult mutate(MLIRContext *ctx, typename T::ImplType *impl,
                              Args &&...args) {
    assert(impl && "cannot mutate null type");
    return ctx->getTypeUniquer().mutate(T::getTypeID(), impl,
                                        std::forward<Args>(args)...);
  }

  /// Register a type instance T with the uniquer.
  template <typename T>
  static void registerType(MLIRContext *ctx) {
    registerType<T>(ctx, T::getTypeID());
  }

  /// Register a parametric type instance T with the uniquer.
  /// The use of this method is in general discouraged in favor of
  /// 'registerType<T>(ctx)'.
  template <typename T>
  static std::enable_if_t<
      !std::is_same<typename T::ImplType, TypeStorage>::value>
  registerType(MLIRContext *ctx, TypeID typeID) {
    ctx->getTypeUniquer().registerParametricStorageType<typename T::ImplType>(
        typeID);
  }
  /// Register a singleton type instance T with the uniquer.
  /// The use of this method is in general discouraged in favor of
  /// 'registerType<T>(ctx)'.
  template <typename T>
  static std::enable_if_t<
      std::is_same<typename T::ImplType, TypeStorage>::value>
  registerType(MLIRContext *ctx, TypeID typeID) {
    ctx->getTypeUniquer().registerSingletonStorageType<TypeStorage>(
        typeID, [&ctx, typeID](TypeStorage *storage) {
          storage->initialize(AbstractType::lookup(typeID, ctx));
        });
  }
};
} // namespace detail

} // namespace mlir

#endif

struct TensorTypeStorage : public ::mlir::TypeStorage {
  using KeyTy = std::tuple<::M::MOSH::ShapeAttr, DType, ::M::DeviceRefAttr, DictionaryAttr>;
  TensorTypeStorage(::M::MOSH::ShapeAttr shape, DType dtype, ::M::DeviceRefAttr deviceRef, DictionaryAttr metadata) : shape(std::move(shape)), dtype(std::move(dtype)), deviceRef(std::move(deviceRef)), metadata(std::move(metadata)) {}

  KeyTy getAsKey() const {
    return KeyTy(shape, dtype, deviceRef, metadata);
  }

  bool operator==(const KeyTy &tblgenKey) const {
    return (shape == std::get<0>(tblgenKey)) && (dtype == std::get<1>(tblgenKey)) && (deviceRef == std::get<2>(tblgenKey)) && (metadata == std::get<3>(tblgenKey));
  }

  static ::llvm::hash_code hashKey(const KeyTy &tblgenKey) {
    return ::llvm::hash_combine(std::get<0>(tblgenKey), std::get<1>(tblgenKey), std::get<2>(tblgenKey), std::get<3>(tblgenKey));
  }

  static TensorTypeStorage *construct(::mlir::TypeStorageAllocator &allocator, KeyTy &&tblgenKey) {
    auto shape = std::move(std::get<0>(tblgenKey));
    auto dtype = std::move(std::get<1>(tblgenKey));
    auto deviceRef = std::move(std::get<2>(tblgenKey));
    auto metadata = std::move(std::get<3>(tblgenKey));
    return new (allocator.allocate<TensorTypeStorage>()) TensorTypeStorage(std::move(shape), std::move(dtype), std::move(deviceRef), std::move(metadata));
  }

  ::M::MOSH::ShapeAttr shape;
  DType dtype;
  ::M::DeviceRefAttr deviceRef;
  DictionaryAttr metadata;
};

} // namespace detail
::llvm::LogicalResult TensorType::verifyInvariants(::llvm::function_ref<::mlir::InFlightDiagnostic()> emitError, ::M::MOSH::ShapeAttr shape, DType dtype, ::M::DeviceRefAttr deviceRef, DictionaryAttr metadata) {
  if (::mlir::failed(verify(emitError, shape, dtype, deviceRef, metadata)))
    return ::mlir::failure();
  return ::mlir::success();
}

::M::MOSH::ShapeAttr TensorType::getShape() const {
  return getImpl()->shape;
}

DType TensorType::getDtype() const {
  return getImpl()->dtype;
}

::M::DeviceRefAttr TensorType::getDeviceRef() const {
  return getImpl()->deviceRef;
}

DictionaryAttr TensorType::getMetadata() const {
  return getImpl()->metadata;
}

::mlir::Type ListType::parse(::mlir::AsmParser &odsParser) {
  ::mlir::Builder odsBuilder(odsParser.getContext());
  ::llvm::SMLoc odsLoc = odsParser.getCurrentLocation();
  (void) odsLoc;
  ::mlir::FailureOr<Type> _result_elementType;
  // Parse literal '<'
  if (odsParser.parseLess()) return {};

  // Parse variable 'elementType'
  _result_elementType = ::mlir::FieldParser<Type>::parse(odsParser);
  if (::mlir::failed(_result_elementType)) {
    odsParser.emitError(odsParser.getCurrentLocation(), "failed to parse MO_List parameter 'elementType' which is to be a `Type`");
    return {};
  }
  // Parse literal '>'
  if (odsParser.parseGreater()) return {};
  assert(::mlir::succeeded(_result_elementType));
  return odsParser.getChecked<ListType>(odsLoc, odsParser.getContext(),
      Type((*_result_elementType)));
}

  ::mlir::Builder odsBuilder(getContext());
  odsPrinter << "<";
  odsPrinter.printStrippedAttrOrType(getElementType());
  odsPrinter << ">";
}
